comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: S2 plan-review v2: BLOCK down to blocking=1 (from 5). Remaining finding [T8] was fair — I named a rebar override table without defining its schema/keys/lookup/precedence/entries. Investigated before inventing one, and found it is LOAD-BEARING not speculative: anthropic_model_profile(claude-opus-4-8).supports_json_schema_output is TRUE (verified), so a naive profile read would flip rebar PRIMARY provider from PromptedOutput to NativeOutput — silently breaking the deliberate choice at structured.py:40-46 AND the existing assertion at test_structured.py:179. SECOND KEY FINDING: Bedrock-hosted Claude gets a BedrockModelProfile, NOT an AnthropicModelProfile (sibling ModelProfile subclasses), yet also reports supports_json_schema_output=True — so an isinstance(AnthropicModelProfile) override alone would MISS the exact models this epic exists to support and Bedrock Claude would wrongly get NativeOutput. Discriminator for Bedrock-hosted Claude is the profile FIELD bedrock_thinking_variant==anthropic (verified: anthropic for Bedrock Claude, openai for Bedrock OpenAI, absent/None for Meta/Amazon) — a capability-field read, materially different from the banned resolved.startswith(anthropic) model-string match. THIRD: I tried an elegant flag-only rule (supports_json_schema_output AND NOT supports_thinking) and TESTED it against every provider in todays _NATIVE_OUTPUT_PROVIDERS — it BREAKS TWO: gemini-2.5-flash has supports_thinking=True and groq has supports_json_schema_output=False, both of which would lose NativeOutput. Rejected it; documented why. Defined the table as an ORDERED (predicate, overrides) tuple (not a name-keyed dict, which would reintroduce string matching and cannot span two hosts of one model family), first-match-wins, overrides applied AFTER profile derivation, with exactly ONE entry (_is_claude covering both hosts). DISCLOSED ONE INTENTIONAL BEHAVIOR CHANGE: groq moves NativeOutput->PromptedOutput because its profile says supports_json_schema_output=False; accepted deliberately (profile is authoritative, groq unreachable via rebar _PAI_PROVIDER_PREFIX, untested, safe direction) and pinned by a test so it is deliberate not incidental. Re-reviewing.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: S2 plan-review v4: blocking=1, and it was the BEST finding yet — a genuine architectural hole S1 created. S1 deliberately leaves openai/google as LAZY MODEL STRINGS (not objects) so their optional SDKs need not be importable. But capabilities_for() reads model.profile, and getattr(str, profile, None) is None -> conservative fallback -> native_structured_output=False -> openai/google SILENTLY lose NativeOutput, which test_structured.py:177 asserts against. RESOLVED with a verified asymmetry: pydantic_ai.profiles.* are PURE capability records that import WITHOUT the vendor SDK (confirmed: openai/google/groq SDKs all ABSENT from the venv, yet openai_model_profile(gpt-4o).supports_json_schema_output returns True), whereas pydantic_ai.providers.openai raises ImportError. So capabilities_for() now accepts a model OBJECT or a model STRING, resolving the latter through a single _PROFILE_RESOLVERS registry into pydantic_ai.profiles.* — rebar can read capabilities for a provider it cannot construct, exactly the asymmetry S1s lazy path needs. Added an AC pinning that a lazy openai:gpt-4o string still yields native_structured_output=True (i.e. the fallback is NOT reached for a merely-deferred provider). Also added runner.py:28 import as an explicit Scope edit target (v3s two duplicate blockers). Re-reviewing.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: S4 (dc0d) plan-review v1: BLOCK blocking=2, and BOTH findings were the SAME real contradiction between S4s plan and what S2 actually built — caught pre-implementation. S4 claimed capability handling comes free from S2 because an opaque endpoint resolves to the CONSERVATIVE record so structured output takes the prompted path. FALSE, verified two ways: (1) capabilities_for() reads .profile off a model OBJECT first and S4s builder produces a real OpenAIChatModel carrying the genuine OpenAI profile; (2) openai_model_profile(local-model).supports_json_schema_output is TRUE, so even the STRING path resolves through _PROFILE_RESOLVERS[openai] to a native-capable record. Either way a local Ollama/LMStudio/vLLM endpoint would get NativeOutput (strict json_schema constrained decoding) which an OpenAI-COMPATIBLE server has no obligation to implement — failure mode is a silent wrong answer or an opaque parse error. The conservative fallback never fires because a key DOES match. FIX: the builder supplies an explicit ModelProfile override — verified OpenAIChatModel.__init__ accepts profile: ModelProfileSpec|None in the pinned pydantic-ai source (same caller-supplied mechanism the epic already uses for Bedrock) — passing dataclasses.replace(openai_model_profile(name), supports_json_schema_output=False). Justification: the OpenAI profile describes OpenAIs HOSTED API; a custom base_url is by definition a DIFFERENT server that merely speaks the same wire protocol, so upstreams strict-output flag is not evidence about it. This makes the plans claim true BY CONSTRUCTION, needs no change to S2s capabilities_for, and adds no per-call boolean (preserving the rejection of PR #121s force_prompted). Added two ACs: the override is actually applied (native_structured_output False => PromptedOutput), and it is SURGICAL (another capability off the same profile is unchanged), so it cannot degenerate into a blanket conservative record.

The tool documents this exact case: --ref REF says pass --ref HEAD when the review depends on code committed locally but not yet landed on the default ref (a stacked change), else symbols it adds read as does-not-exist FALSE FINDINGS. I was not using it. This likely inflated S2s six review passes too. Switching to --ref HEAD; NO early land needed (I had considered submitting S1+S2 early to fix the ref, which would have been the wrong tool for this). Finding 1 (E4) was a GENUINE correction: my plan asserted the openai SDK is not installed, which I made false myself by pip-installing it for the dev extra. Reworded to the accurate claim (not a RUNTIME dependency; agents extra omits it; dev only) and — more importantly — replaced the rationale so it no longer depends on SDK absence at all: with no base_url configured rebar has NOTHING to contribute to provider construction (no endpoint, no key, no profile override), so interposing a builder that merely reconstructs what pydantic-ai would build adds maintenance surface and divergence risk for zero benefit. rebar builds a provider only when it has configuration to apply — the same rule S1 established for Anthropic (it injects a retrying transport).

Findings: (1) on-demand model ids are NOT invokable at all here (ValidationException, both modern and old models) so S3s on-demand-vs-profile comparison is moot — only inference profiles work; (2) us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 CACHES (cache_write=4017 then cache_read=4017, reproducible across runs via a warm 5-min TTL cache) which REFUTES pydantic-ai #4381s premise for this model/region; (3) caching is MODEL-dependent and fails SILENTLY — us. AND global. opus-4-5 both report cache_read=0 and cache_write=0 while billing the full 4029 input tokens, and a controlled same-model us-vs-global comparison REFUTED MY OWN first inference that the global. prefix was the cause; (4) Haiku 3 + cachePoint hard-fails AccessDenied. (5) NEW HIGH-SEVERITY not in the plan: temperature is FATAL on Bedrock for some models — us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7 + temperature=0 returns 400 temperature is deprecated for this model, confirmed through pydantic-ai as ModelHTTPError 400, and _drop_unsupported_sampling_settings exists ONLY in pydantic-ais models/anthropic.py not models/bedrock.py, so the Anthropic path degrades with a warning and Bedrock hard-fails. rebar sets temperature whenever configured and its Pass-2 verifiers deliberately send temperature=0, so Bedrock gate runs would break — and this directly threatens eb6e (prod cutover, no fallback). Plan now carries three DECISIONS rather than open questions: default = us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6; warn when caching requested but both counters zero (mirroring _warn_if_zeroed_usage); carry supports_temperature on f184s capability record with a Bedrock override entry and omit the parameter when withdrawn (rejected: dropping temperature on all Bedrock calls, which loses Pass-2 greedy determinism; and catch-400-and-retry, which burns a billable agentic call on model-specific error text). Also resolved the 3-vs-2 cache-key contradiction in favour of TWO keys for parity with the Anthropic path, and moved the builder to a NEW leaf src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py because providers.py is at 289 against a 300 cap that is an ATTESTED criterion of closed story 7468.

## AWS — READ THIS BEFORE ANY MEASUREMENT
Profile `frontier` NOW points at the PROJECT account 896586841071 / us-east-1 as user/joe_frontier,
which holds AdministratorAccess (I added it to the Admin group at the operator's request).

Verified in the project account: on-demand model ids are NOT invokable (ValidationException, use inference
profiles); us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 CACHES (cache_write=4017 then cache_read=4017); us./global.

CRITICAL VERIFICATION RULE, learned the hard way twice: do NOT validate a scoped IAM grant from an
identity holding bedrock:* or AdministratorAccess — a wildcard cannot fail. And do NOT stop at
`aws iam simulate-principal-policy`: it answers what the policy permits for the action you NAMED, not
which action the service CHECKS. The Converse API authorizes against bedrock:InvokeModel, NOT
bedrock:Converse — the simulator said otherwise and was wrong; only a real call from the instance
(SSM, i-00880b2c7f13527c5) settled it. Full recipe: infra/runbooks/bedrock-access.md.

## Gate mechanics that cost time in this run
- review-plan and the claim/close gates default to --ref origin/main, which PREDATES this unsubmitted
  stack, producing false "symbol does not exist" findings. Use `rebar review-plan <id> --ref HEAD` and
  `REBAR_GATE_REF=HEAD rebar claim/transition ...`. This is documented in --help; not knowing it cost
  several review rounds.
- The completion-verifier reads COMMITTED state. Uncommitted tests read as missing.
- Criteria whose evidence is external must be tagged [operator-attested] and cite a change id + vote, or
  the verifier cannot credit them.
- Do NOT mutate the working tree while a gating suite runs in it: conftest's pytest_sessionfinish
  escalates a clean run to exit 1 if git status gains entries (I tripped this by running terraform).
- Store lock contention with other sessions is normal; retry rather than force.
